events.title: 2026 south-west monsoon ends 12.6% below normal (87% of LPA), driest since 2015
events.description: IMD: June-Sept rainfall 759.4 mm vs 868.6 mm LPA (1971-2020), i.e. 87% of LPA / -12.6%. Lowest since 2015 (758.2 mm); fourth-lowest since 2001. Monthly: June 65% of normal, July ~101% (central India +33%), August 84%, September 92.4%. East and North-East India recorded its driest monsoon since 1901 (1,017.1 mm). 282 districts (38%) deficient; 15 states below normal; drought declared in parts of Maharashtra and Karnataka; South peninsula ~-23% by 28 Sep. IMD had forecast 92% of LPA (13 Apr) cut to 90% (29 May), so the aggregate was anticipated but June was far worse than forecast. Strong El Nino in progress (IMD 30 Sep: strong El Nino over equatorial Pacific, expected to strengthen through end-2026 and peak ~Nov); Indian Ocean Dipole neutral, i.e. no positive-IOD offset.
events.what_already_moved: Aggregate was forecast since April, so little index reaction; downstream moves: Indian sugar +27.8% since 1 Jun (global ICE raw sugar, factor_state), Nifty FMCG hit fresh 52-week low (Dalal Street Investment Journal, Oct 2026), India food CPI 7.74% in Sep from 5.52% in Jul.

entry_shocks.note: Season total -12.6% vs LPA; SSU is +10% so -1.26 SSU.
Deficient rain raises irrigation pumping and cooling load; small positive (low confidence).

chains.explanation: Lower kharif output (rice, pulses, oilseeds, vegetables) lifts food prices; see EV_FOOD_CPI_SEP26 for the realised level.

events.title: Strong El Nino of 2026-27 peaking around Nov-Dec 2026
events.description: IMD (30 Sep 2026 press conference): strong El Nino conditions prevail over the equatorial Pacific, with SSTs significantly above average in the east-central and eastern Pacific; IMD MMCFS and global models indicate further strengthening through end-2026 (press talk of a 'super El Nino'; Indian Express 14 Aug: strongest in decades possible by year-end). IOD neutral and forecast to stay neutral through the north-east monsoon. IMD expected October rain below normal. Historically El Nino also lifts hot, dry winter-spring risk for rabi crops (heat at grain fill in Feb-Mar) and depresses the next monsoon only if it persists into spring; by April-May 2027 it usually decays.
events.what_already_moved: ENSO status itself not a traded price; downstream moves captured in monsoon, food-inflation and sugar events.

entry_shocks.note: Incremental forward effect: raises odds of weak post-monsoon rain and a warm rabi season; avoids double-counting the realised monsoon deficit by keeping the shock small.

events.title: Kharif 2026 output hit: paddy area down, foodgrain target cut, rice output seen sharpest fall in ~2 decades
events.description: Agriculture Ministry (29 Sep) set a 2026-27 foodgrain target of 373.93 MT vs 376.56 MT estimated for 2025-26 (-0.7%), with a rabi target of 177.72 MT vs 174.51 MT actual; a first (kharif) advance estimate is not yet published (usually Sept-Oct; not found). Kharif acreage reached 1,056.7 lakh ha by 25 Aug (record-ish headline) but paddy area was ~4% lower in mid-Sep (about 1.7 mn ha less than a year ago: Karnataka -454k ha, Telangana -446k, AP -190k, MP -175k, TN -140k, Maharashtra -115k). Reuters (17 Sep): India rice output faces the biggest drop in two decades, though FCI stocks cushion exports (article behind paywall; magnitude not verified). Central Pool grain stocks 925.85 LMT on 1 Jul 2026 vs buffer norm 411.2 LMT (Business Today 8 Oct).

events.title: Reservoir storage at multi-year low after weak monsoon (south India worst)
events.description: CWC bulletin of 15 Oct 2026: 178 major reservoirs hold 126.717 BCM = 68.58% of live capacity, 41.19 BCM (24.5%) below the same date last year and ~24.9 BCM below the 10-year average. On 24 Sep, storage was 70% vs 10-yr average 76.62% and 79% in 2025 (Indian Express: lowest in 10 years). South India (AP, Telangana, Karnataka, Kerala, TN) was at ~50% vs 87% a year ago; Pennar and Cauvery basins are most stressed (Mettur, Somasila, Aliyar critical), while Narmada and Mahanadi basins have surplus. Raises rabi irrigation, drinking-water and hydropower risks for Jan-Jun 2027.
events.what_already_moved: No direct price series; supports weak rabi sowing (EV_RABI_SOWING_LAG26) and hydro generation shortfall.

entry_shocks.note: Carry-over effect on irrigation-dependent rabi crop (kept small to avoid double count with EV_SWMONSOON26_DEFICIT).

events.title: Food-led inflation spike: CPI 5.54% and food CPI 7.74% in Sep 2026; WPI 11.39% (series high)
events.description: MoSPI (12 Oct, new base 2024=100): headline CPI 5.54% in Sep vs 4.83% in Aug and 4.45% in Jul (23-month high on comparable basis); food inflation 7.74% vs 5.97% in Aug and 5.52% in Jul; rural 6.08% vs urban 4.88% (rural up from 5.24%). Onion retail prices roughly doubled y/y (NDTV; ToI: 41 of 42 essential commodities up y/y, onion +113%, tomato +59% y/y per AgroSpectrum). WPI (14 Oct): 11.39% y/y in Sep from 9.9% in Aug, a series high, on food, fuel and manufactured goods; WPI food was 7.1% in Aug (20-month high) on vegetables, milk, spices, edible oils and sugar; core WPI 8.1%. RBI Oct bulletin: broad-based food price increase. RBI projected FY27 CPI at 5.2% on 7 Oct. Reuters: print boosts the case for further hikes. Milk: Karnataka (Nandini) raised milk Rs 8/l from 1 Nov; Aavin products up to 25% and Amul ghee/butter up (reports).

events.title: Rabi sowing sharply behind: 37.56 lakh ha vs 69.02 lakh ha a year ago; wheat 0.19 lakh ha vs 3.34
events.description: Agriculture Ministry data as of 30 Oct 2026 (Business Today, 3 Nov): total rabi area 37.56 lakh ha (-45.6%); wheat 0.19 vs 3.34 lakh ha; pulses 9.45 vs 19.56 (gram 5.90 vs 14.35); oilseeds 20.97 vs 38.62 (rapeseed-mustard 20.50 vs 38.07); coarse cereals 3.78 vs 4.22. Causes: inadequate soil moisture, high daytime temperature, limited irrigation/canal water. Wheat is normally sown Oct-Nov (full season 336 lakh ha in 2025-26) so the lag is recoverable until about 15 Dec, but the sowing window and soil-moisture constraints are real. Government's rabi target is 177.72 MT. Business Standard (24 Oct) had expected wheat acreage steady; actual early data weaker. Rajasthan sowing delayed (BS, 2 Nov).
events.what_already_moved: Wheat (CBOT proxy) -14.7% 1m (factor_state), mostly the global Black-Sea/export-ban context; domestic prices not yet moved on sowing news (not verified).

entry_shocks.note: Early sowing lag adds a small risk premium; global wheat already -1.3% since 1 Jun.

events.title: India cuts edible-oil import duties from 24 Sep 2026 (crude palm/soy 10% to 5%, crude sunflower to zero)
events.description: Notification of 23 Sep, effective 24 Sep: basic customs duty on crude palm and soya oil 10% to 5%; refined palm/soy 32.5% to 27.5%; crude sunflower 10% to 0%; refined sunflower 32.5% to 22.5%. Rationale: sharp rise in food inflation before festivals (WPI food 7.1% in Aug, edible oils among drivers). Government asked companies to pass on the cut. Oils & Fats International expects sunflower oil imports +30% in 2026/27. Duty had been raised in Sep 2024 and halved on crude oils in May 2025 (model knowledge).

events.title: Sugar supply shock: 2025-26 output cut to ~306 lakh t, retail sugar at record, first duty-free raw sugar imports in a decade
events.description: Food ministry (21-22 Aug): 2025-26 (Oct-Sep) sugar output ~306 lakh t, 11% below the 343 lakh t initial projection; opening stock 1 Oct 2026 ~33-34 lakh t vs 50 lakh t a year earlier. Retail sugar Rs 58.2/kg, +20% in a month and +26% y/y. DGFT (20 Aug) allowed duty-free import of 10 lakh t raw sugar under a TRQ until 31 Oct; stockholding limits on bulk traders were considered; fortnightly sale quotas to mills from September; mills told to report output monthly (Oct). ISMA (24-26 Aug, 26 Oct) says no shortage and that stocks are sufficient; 107 mills began crushing 2026-27 by 26 Oct. FRP for 2026-27 raised only Rs 10/q; mills and ISMA seek a sugar MSP (minimum selling price, Rs 31/kg since 2019 - model knowledge) increase; Karnataka cane farmers protesting. Centre set up a panel to review sugar prices/farmers' payments. Global raw sugar (ICE proxy) +27.8% since 1 Jun but -11.3% in 1m (18.47 c/lb on 5 Nov).
events.what_already_moved: ICE sugar: +27.0% 6m, +27.8% since 2026-06-01, -11.3% 1m, +18.6% 3m (factor_state); Indian retail +26% y/y.

entry_shocks.note: Realised +27.8% since 1 Jun in ICE raw sugar (SSU +10%); Indian ex-mill prices rose similarly.
Policy tilted against millers: duty-free imports, stock limits, ethanol diversion curbed (see ethanol event).

events.title: OMC ethanol tender ESY 2026-27: no cane juice/syrup/B-heavy ethanol; maize price incentive cut; grain-based ethanol takes over
events.description: Oil marketing companies invited bids for 1,100 crore litres of ethanol for Nov 2026-Oct 2027 while barring sugarcane juice, sugar syrup and B-heavy molasses (CNBC-TV18 17 Oct; Hindu/ToI 18 Oct), i.e. zero sugar diversion; last year about 289 crore litres were initially allocated to cane-based feedstocks. Maize-ethanol incentive cut from Rs 5.79 to Rs 2.79/l, taking maize ethanol to Rs 68.86/l; broken-rice/damaged-food-grain ethanol priced at Rs 64/l; a feedstock-switch clause pays the lower price. Industry expects DFG/broken rice ethanol to rise from ~80 to >700 crore litres, raising competition with food/feed and maize. Grain ethanol is ~76% of supply (AIDA, July). Grain distillers pushing for price revision (FE, 2 Nov). Government argues (Aug) that only ~9% of sugar was diverted in 2025-26 and about 75% of ethanol is grain-based.
events.what_already_moved: F_SUGAR -11.3% over 1m to 5 Nov after the tender and imports; no distiller equity move quantified.

entry_shocks.note: Policy shift against sugar-based ethanol (negative for mills' distillery profits; positive for sugar availability).
More sugar available for the domestic market, lower domestic sugar prices.

chains.explanation: Zero diversion adds ~30-35 lakh t sugar to supply (289 crore litres cane-based), cooling prices.

events.title: Government lifts wheat and wheat-product export ban (24 Aug 2026)
events.description: DGFT notification (24 Aug): wheat (incl. durum) export policy revised from 'prohibited' to 'free' with immediate effect; wheat flour, maida, semolina also freed. Follows limited permission in Feb 2026. Rationale: farmers' interests amid depressed local prices after record 2025-26 crop (120.6 MT per Bloomberg) and record projected stocks (USDA); Black Sea/war disruption lifted global prices. Bangladesh sought Indian wheat. Since then monsoon failure and rabi sowing lag (wheat 0.19 vs 3.34 lakh ha on 30 Oct) raise the risk of reversal.

FMCG: Oct value growth reported at 15% (India Business Trade); Q2 FY27 demand resilient but analysts flag H2 risk from weakest monsoon since 2015 and input inflation (BusinessLine 16 Oct); Patanjali Foods holding 15% FMCG growth guidance despite rural weakness. Rural CPI 6.08% (Sep) vs urban 4.88%. VB-G RAM G (replacement for MGNREGA): person-days fell about 50% in first month, -61% in July (BS/Indian Express, Aug), partly sowing pause. Smaller FMCG firms squeezed by costs and slowing rural demand (ET, 5 Nov). Rural wage data (Labour Bureau) not retrieved: data gap.

events.description: Industry estimates (RuralVoice, 2 Oct): subsidy could reach Rs 3 lakh crore in FY27; gas for urea rose from ~US$15 to ~US$28/MMBtu after the Iran-US war; domestic urea cost >Rs 62,000/t; DAP >US$900/t; sulphur ~US$900/t with supply below normal (Qatar gas/sulphur disruptions). events.title: India 2027 wheat crop (harvest Mar-Apr 2027) below 2026's record ~120 MT
events.description: 2025-26 wheat crop was a record ~120.6 MT (Bloomberg, Aug 2026). 2027 crop faces: wheat sown 0.19 vs 3.34 lakh ha at 30 Oct (full season ~336 lakh ha last year), poor soil moisture and low reservoirs, an El Nino winter with heat risk at grain fill. Recovery is possible if sowing accelerates in Nov (soil moisture, mid-Nov cooler weather) and if irrigation holds in Punjab/Haryana/UP (canal-irrigated, groundwater-fed, not rain-dependent). I put 65% on 2027 output below 2026 (central estimate 108-116 MT) and 25% on a fall >8%. Central Pool stocks (925.85 LMT on 1 Jul) cushion availability so the effect is mainly sentiment/price, not scarcity. Government rabi target 177.72 MT.

events.title: India re-imposes curbs on broken-rice exports
events.description: IREF warned on 3 Nov that India may re-impose restrictions on 100% broken rice exports as international prices cross US$360/t and domestic demand rises from ethanol distillers and poultry feed. No curbs announced yet. The ethanol tender (zero sugar diversion; broken rice priced Rs 64/l) could pull large volumes of broken rice into fuel; Reuters flagged the biggest rice output drop in ~2 decades. Offsetting factor: huge Central Pool rice stocks. Probability 35% by early Feb; 45% by Nov 2027.

events.title: Sugar minimum selling price raised above Rs 31/kg (or panel recommends)
events.description: Industry (ISMA) seeks timely alignment of sugar MSP (unchanged at Rs 31/kg since Feb 2019, model knowledge) with FRP (+Rs 10/q for 2026-27) and ethanol prices; Centre set up a panel to review sugar prices and farmers' payments; Karnataka cane farmers are protesting for higher cane price and sugar MSP. Retail sugar at Rs 58/kg is far above MSP, so the government has little reason to raise MSP while prices are high; a hike becomes likelier if prices fall as cane crushing (107 mills started) gets going and ethanol diversion is zero. Probability 20% by end-Jan 2027, 40% by Nov 2027.

events.title: IMD April 2027 long-range forecast says normal or above-normal monsoon (>=96% LPA)
events.description: Strong El Nino typically peaks in Nov-Jan and decays by spring; the next monsoon is often normal after a deficient year but not guaranteed (e.g. 2015-16: 2016 normal at 97%). IMD first forecast usually mid-April, update end-May. Probability that the first forecast is >=96% LPA: 68%; 'below normal' (<96%): 32%, which includes re-intensifying El Nino or negative IOD signals. Prior model-based judgement; ENSO forecasts for spring 2027 not yet retrievable.
